data.body_html:
Taking your kids on a dolphin watching boat trip in Marbella is one of the most memorable family experiences you can have on the Costa del Sol. With calm Mediterranean waters, a coastline dotted with coves, and a good chance of spotting wild dolphins, it's an adventure that blends excitement with relaxation. This guide covers everything you need to know—from choosing the right boat to safety tips and what to expect on the day.

Why Marbella is Great for Dolphin Watching with Kids

Marbella's coastline, stretching from Puerto Banús to Cabopino, offers a rich marine ecosystem. Dolphins are frequently seen in the waters between Marbella and Estepona, especially in the early morning. The sea is generally calm from May to October, with water temperatures around 20-25°C, making it comfortable for children. The proximity of the Sierra Blanca mountains and La Concha peak creates a stunning backdrop that adds to the magic of the trip.

Choosing the Right Boat for Your Family

Not all boats are equally suitable for children. For a family of up to 9, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) is a stable and spacious choice, departing from Puerto Banús. If you have a slightly larger group (up to 11), the Azimut 39 (12.5m) offers similar comfort. Both are part of our Tier A pricing: €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, all inclusive. For a more intimate experience with just your immediate family, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is perfect—small enough to feel personal but safe and reliable.

For larger family gatherings or if you want extra luxury, consider the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski for older kids. All our boats are maintained to high safety standards and include a licensed skipper who knows the best dolphin spots.

What's Included in Your Charter

Every charter with us includes everything you need for a stress-free trip:

  • Licensed skipper (experienced with families)
  • Fuel for the entire trip
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Light snacks (chips, nuts, fruit)
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

You don't need to bring anything except sunscreen and a sense of adventure. For kids, we provide life jackets in various sizes, and the skipper will give a safety briefing before departure.

Best Times and Routes for Dolphin Sightings

Dolphins are most active in the early morning (8-10 AM) or late afternoon (4-6 PM). We recommend booking a 2-hour trip in the morning—it's long enough to find dolphins but not too tiring for young children. Common routes head west from Puerto Banús towards Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, or east towards Cabopino. These areas are known for dolphin pods, and skippers often spot them within 20-30 minutes of leaving the marina.

If you want a longer adventure, a 4-hour trip allows you to combine dolphin watching with a swim stop in a quiet cove. Remember, we never chase or harass dolphins—we maintain a respectful distance, which is both ethical and safer for kids.

Safety Tips for Kids on a Boat

Safety is paramount. Here are our top tips:

  • Always have kids wear life jackets, especially if they can't swim well.
  • Keep children seated while the boat is moving; they can stand when anchored or drifting.
  • Apply sunscreen generously (SPF 50+) and reapply every 2 hours.
  • Bring a light jacket—sea breezes can be cool even in summer.
  • If your child is prone to seasickness, give them motion sickness medication 30 minutes before departure (consult your doctor).

Our skippers are trained to handle family groups and will slow down or change course if anyone feels uncomfortable.

Booking and Pricing

Prices for our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are fixed: €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours, all inclusive. For the Mangusta 80 (including the grey variant), the price is €4,719 for a minimum of 4 hours, with a free jet ski. For other boats in our fleet, such as the Ferretti 94 or Pershing 46, prices are available on request via WhatsApp—just contact us with your preferred dates and group size.

Book at least 2-3 days in advance, especially in July and August, as family-friendly slots fill up quickly. You can reserve via our website or WhatsApp, and we'll confirm availability within hours.

What to Expect on the Day

On the day, arrive at Puerto Banús 15 minutes early. Your skipper will greet you, give a safety briefing, and help everyone onboard. As you cruise out, keep your eyes on the water—dolphins often surf the bow wave, which delights kids. The skipper will point out any sightings and share fun facts about the local marine life. After dolphin watching, you might stop for a swim in a calm cove, depending on the trip duration.

Don't forget your camera—but also take time to just watch. The joy on your kids' faces when they see a dolphin leap is priceless. For more ideas on family-friendly boating, check out our [main guide to boat rentals in Marbella](/).
